scenes.text: Henry Ford cut the time to build a car chassis from over twelve hours to ninety three minutes.
His secret was the moving assembly line.
Before, each Model T was built in one spot, with workers bringing parts to it.
The idea came from Chicago meatpackers, who moved carcasses past workers on overhead trolleys.
Ford's team tested it in early nineteen thirteen on a small part called the magneto.
In October nineteen thirteen, they tried it on the whole chassis at the Highland Park plant.
About one hundred forty workers lined a one hundred fifty foot track.
Soon a chassis took under three hours, and within about a year, just ninety three minutes.
At its peak, the line turned out one Model T every twenty four seconds.
Cars got cheaper too, from eight hundred fifty dollars at launch to under three hundred.
Over fifteen million Model Ts were built by nineteen twenty seven, nearly half the cars sold worldwide till then.
Would you rather build a whole car, or do one job all day? Tell me below.

title: Ford cut car building from 12 hours to 93 minutes 🚗
caption: In 1913 Ford's Highland Park plant put the Model T chassis on a moving assembly line, inspired by Chicago meatpackers. Build time fell from over 12 hours to 93 minutes, and more than 15 million Model Ts were made.
